solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Thought again about beliefs leader expressed about prayer

indicators.note: the second about means going round, so the shortened beliefs word wraps the prayer
expressed in its old sense of pressed out: the leading letter of the word for beliefs is squeezed away

parts.note: a creed is a statement of beliefs
a collect is a short prayer in Anglican and Catholic services

explanation.surface: Someone reconsiders a set of beliefs after a leader voiced them over a prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'about' belongs to the definition; only the second is the container. 'expressed' is used in its old sense of squeezed out, which gets rid of the leading letter. A collect is a short church prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: To recollect is to recall or call back to mind, a fair sense of thinking again about something.

clue.text: In period of rule fool is set aside afresh

indicators.note: in signals that the word for a fool sits inside the word for a period of rule

parts.note: a reign is the period a monarch rules
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: During a reign, a foolish courtier is pushed aside once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' simply links wordplay to definition; 'afresh' belongs with 'set aside' as the re- of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign is to allot or earmark, so doing it again means earmarking something anew.

clue.text: Writer who may have something to offer in dark times

definitions.text: who may have something to offer in dark times
definitions.meaning: a candle maker or seller, whose wares help when it is dark

explanation.surface: An author with consolation for people going through bleak days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark times' sounds like hardship, but here it means literally unlit hours, when candles are wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler wrote noir crime fiction; a chandler is also a candle dealer, handy at night.

clue.text: Boundary must be illuminated — this person's brought in

indicators.note: brought in says the short form for I am is placed inside the word for illuminated

parts.note: lit means illuminated
this person is the speaker, so this person's stands for I'm, I am

explanation.surface: A border must be lit up when I am brought in to patrol it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this person's' is 'this person is', the setter speaking: I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is an edge or bound beyond which one cannot go, the same idea as a boundary.

clue.text: Journalist eating lunch maybe — right inside stone is found

indicators.note: eating means the journalist's letters take in the rest, wrapping round it

parts.note: ED is the usual short form for editor, a journalist

indicators.note: inside places the letter for right within the meal word

parts.note: lunch is an example of a meal

explanation.surface: A reporter at lunch finds a gemstone inside his food.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'inside' puts the right letter into the meal, then 'eating' has the journalist wrap the lot. 'is found' is linking text.
explanation.definitionFit: An emerald is a green precious gem, a type of precious stone.

clue.text: Growth of vegetation is just what you want outside hospital

indicators.note: outside says the idiom's word goes around the hospital letter

parts.note: the ticket is an idiom for exactly the thing needed
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A patch of greenery is exactly what's wanted outside a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just the ticket' is a British idiom for just what is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A thicket is a dense mass of shrubs and small trees, a tangle of plant growth.

clue.text: The Lord's Day's calm — I repeatedly nod off

indicators.note: off signals the letters are thrown out of order and rearranged
repeatedly tells us to take the letter I twice

explanation.surface: Sunday is so peaceful that I keep dozing off.
explanation.walkthrough: CALM, I twice and NOD are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominical is an adjective meaning to do with Sunday, from Latin dominicus, of the Lord.

clue.text: It's bound to be hard work

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A grim assertion that something is sure to be laborious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to be' reads as 'certain to be', but 'bound' is the definition, a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A hop is a small jump or leap, the same as a bound.

clue.text: Setter maybe going after much- approved food

indicators.note: going after places the setter word behind the approved word

parts.note: hot means popular, in great demand
a setter is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A crossword setter goes looking for some hugely popular food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' tempts as the crossword compiler; here it is the gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot dog is a sausage in a bun, a popular snack food.

clue.text: Watch choice film

parts.note: a pick is a choice, as in take your pick
ET, Spielberg's film about an extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: Keep an eye out for a top film selection.
explanation.definitionFit: A picket is a guard or sentry post, someone keeping watch, as in military usage.

clue.text: Leader of US gang, member creating panic

parts.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster boss
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: An American gang boss and one of his crew cause a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' suggests a first letter, U, but the gang leader is Al Capone.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is sudden fear or dismay, a state close to panic.

clue.text: When troubled, I get manic, hard to understand

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that when worried they become frenzied and baffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enigmatic is puzzling or mysterious, difficult to interpret.

clue.text: Divert footpath?

definitions.meaning: to deflect someone from the main issue or course
a footpath could be called a ..., a minor way off the main road

explanation.surface: A question about rerouting walkers along a path.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidetrack is to distract or turn aside; read in two words it is a byway, a minor path.

clue.text: Loop with knots daughter's got rid of

indicators.note: got rid of means the daughter letter is taken out

parts.note: nodose means having knots or knobs, knotty
D is the abbreviation for daughter, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A rope loop whose knots the girl has undone.
explanation.walkthrough: NODOSE is a rare botanical word for knotty; removing D gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope with a running knot that tightens when pulled.

clue.text: A society beset by avarice given more freedom of action?

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the greed word closes around the pieces

parts.note: greed is avarice

explanation.surface: A community surrounded by greed is allowed more liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the figurative sense: greasing the wheels frees things to move.
explanation.definitionFit: Something greased is lubricated so it moves more easily, playfully put as more freedom of movement.

clue.text: Surprised but not all at once

definitions.meaning: spread out in stages or at different times

explanation.surface: Amazed, though the amazement came gradually.
explanation.definitionFit: Staggered means astounded, and also arranged at intervals rather than simultaneously.

clue.text: Course of inferior food?

definitions.meaning: a line of travel, as when a sailing boat changes direction
poor-quality food, as in hard ..., the ship's biscuit

explanation.surface: A question about a meal course of poor fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests a dish at dinner, but it is a sailing direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A tack is a heading taken by a sailing vessel; tack is also slang for cheap or rough food.

clue.text: She, putting the fellow off, hangs around and behaves amorously

indicators.note: the fellow is he, and putting him off removes those letters from the word she

parts.note: to mooch is to loiter aimlessly

explanation.surface: A woman drops her man, loiters about and gets flirtatious.
explanation.walkthrough: SHE without HE leaves S.
explanation.definitionFit: To smooch is to kiss and cuddle, showing affection in an amorous way.

clue.text: Puzzle's trick discovered

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
found means discovered

explanation.surface: A crossword's deception has been uncovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puzzle's' is 'Puzzle is', so the 's links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To confound is to bewilder or perplex, the verb sense of puzzle.

clue.text: Swag from big room reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for a big room is heard, not seen

parts.note: a hall is a large room

explanation.surface: Loot taken from a grand chamber, so the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A haul is a quantity of stolen goods, which is what swag means in thieves' slang.

clue.text: Picking up one paper for Heather to collect

indicators.note: to collect means the heather word gathers up the other pieces inside it

parts.note: ling is a name for common heather
I is the Roman numeral one
FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a newspaper for a woman called Heather to pick up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a name, but it is the plant LING.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting means raising or picking something up off the ground.

clue.text: Look to get into musical band in capital city

indicators.note: to get into says the look word goes inside the band word

parts.note: a combo is a small jazz or pop band
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Try to join a band playing in a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Colombo is the chief city and commercial capital of Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Contemporary baddie torn apart

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible scoundrel
rent means torn

explanation.surface: A modern villain gets ripped to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Current means belonging to the present time, the sense of contemporary as modern.

clue.text: Sturdy old boy in game on street

indicators.note: in places the old boy letters inside the game letters

parts.note: RU is rugby union
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A tough former pupil plays a game out in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means the street letters come below, after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust means strong and healthy, able to withstand hard use, like sturdy.

clue.text: A Norse god less hairy

definitions.meaning: ..., son of Odin, killed by mistletoe
having less hair on the head, comparative of a word meaning hairless

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian deity who is thinning on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Balder is the Norse god of light, and balder is also the comparative of bald.

clue.text: Primate's holy book, apart from the introduction, good

indicators.note: apart from the introduction says the opening letter of the holy book is dropped

parts.note: the Koran is the holy book of Islam

explanation.surface: An ape's holy text, minus its preface, is good.
explanation.walkthrough: KORAN loses K for ORAN; 'Primate's' is 'Primate is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Orang is short for orang-utan, the great ape of Borneo and Sumatra.

clue.text: Female agent keeping one top position in some way indestructible

indicators.note: keeping says the female and agent letters hold the letter for one

parts.note: rep is short for representative, a sales agent
I is the Roman numeral one
a roof is the topmost part of a building

explanation.surface: A woman spy holding one rooftop spot proves somehow unbeatable.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside F plus REP to make FIREP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fireproof cannot be burnt, so it is indestructible in one particular way.

clue.text: Piece of glass left to form part of door?

parts.note: a pane is a sheet of glass in a window

explanation.surface: A glass pane left over to make part of a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel is a flat section set into a door's frame; the question mark admits other panels exist.

clue.text: Beneath bomb is wreck

parts.note: under means beneath
a mine is an explosive device, a kind of bomb

explanation.surface: An explosive below ground causes devastation.
explanation.definitionFit: To undermine is to weaken or sabotage something, effectively ruining it.

clue.text: Former PM showing hunger for reform, head of government missed

indicators.note: for reform means the remaining letters are reshaped into a new order
missed means that leading letter is left out of the fodder
head of picks out the first letter of government

explanation.surface: An ex-prime minister hungry for change, though the government's head is absent.
explanation.walkthrough: HUNGER without G leaves HUNER, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first prime minister of independent India.

clue.text: Man in boat in unnamed lake

indicators.note: unnamed means losing the N that abbreviates name

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake

explanation.surface: A sailor afloat on a lake nobody has named.
explanation.walkthrough: TARN, a northern English word for a small mountain lake, drops N.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar is old slang for a sailor, a man who serves on board ship.

clue.text: Maybe one meets crazy ladies under the influence of drug

parts.note: one is an example of a digit

indicators.note: crazy means wild, so the letters of ladies are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man meets some wild women while he is high on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' makes ALISED from LADIES. The drug is digitalis, a heart medicine from foxgloves.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitalised describes a patient treated with digitalis until its effect is established.
